candidates.title: Donnie Darko
candidates.reason: A jet engine with no traceable origin, Frank's countdown, visions of predetermined paths and a time-travel text keep the central causal puzzle active throughout the film. Donnie's inquiry into the anomalous events and his apparent manipulation gradually reveal a causal knot, with a timeline reversal providing substantial resolution. The film is unusually surreal and structurally driven by questions about reality and temporal rules. Weaknesses: high-school, family and romantic drama occupy meaningful stretches; several mechanisms remain interpretively ambiguous in the theatrical cut, and Roger Ebert explicitly found the final payoff less satisfying than the setup. The director's cut explains more but is a different edit. Scores describe the original film, with moderate confidence on precise revelation cadence and visual-era presentation.
